$comment: DEBT-SEC-5. Subresource integrity for the third-party libraries this
repository RECOMMENDS but does NOT serve. dist/lib-manifest.json is the
sibling of this file and makes a different promise: it covers assets
scripts/vendor-closure.mjs builds and this origin serves. These are
chosen by the host page, so the guarantee here is the hash of a named
immutable build, not custody of the bytes.
Hashes are recorded rather than computed at build time, deliberately.
A network fetch inside the build gate makes CI non-hermetic and flaky.
jsdelivr versioned URLs are immutable, so a mismatch is an incident and
not drift. Run `npm run sri:verify` to refetch and diff.
CodeMirror 6 is absent on purpose. See the codemirror6 key below.

marked.note: The only required entry. MarkdownRenderer cannot parse without it.

highlight.js-theme.note: Declares no @font-face, so the hash covers the whole stylesheet.

katex-css.closure: stylesheet hashed; the 60 @font-face files it pulls are not SRI-able
katex-css.note: Same residual dist/lib-manifest.json records for bootstrap-icons.

mermaid.note: Mermaid 12 is published. This stays at 11 until the upgrade is reviewed.

mathlive.closure: script hashed; fonts load from fontsDirectory relative to the script and are not SRI-able
mathlive.note: LatexEditor documented 0.107.3/dist/mathlive.min.js, which 404s twice over. That version was never published and the asset is at the package root, not under dist/. ADR-191.

viz.note: The standalone build embeds its WASM, so it fetches nothing at runtime.

driver.js.closure: script hashed; the stylesheet below is a separate entry and carries its own hash
driver.js.note: 1.4.0 and not the 1.4.1 the README named, because 1.4.1 was never published: the 1.4.x line stops at 1.4.0 and both 1.4.1 URLs return 404. The three demo pages were already on 1.4.0.

driver.js-css.closure: complete; this stylesheet pulls no fonts and no further assets

$comment: EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE POINT. This key held codemirror6 from
DEBT-SEC-5 until 2026-10-20, on the reasoning that an integrity
attribute attaches to a script tag and cannot attach to an import
specifier inside a module. That reasoning was correct and the
conclusion did not follow: the fix was never to hash a specifier,
it was to STOP HAVING specifiers. ADR-211 bundles the fourteen
packages into one self-contained file and hashes the file.
The old entry said a consumer needing the guarantee could bundle
CodeMirror themselves or serve it from an origin they control, and
that 'neither is something this repository can do on their behalf'.
Both were things this repository could do, and it has now done the
first. Before adding anything here, check whether the same is true
of it.
